meaning: Together, at the same moment.
cue: Two friends begin to speak at one moment.
reply: Sorry, we both started talking at the same time.
replyJapanese: ごめん、二人同時に話し始めちゃったね。
transferCue: Someone talks to you while you are cooking.
transferReply: I can't cook and talk at the same time.
transferReplyJapanese: 料理とおしゃべりを同時にはできません。
frame: Do two things at the same time
nuance: Use at and keep the: not in same time. It usually comes at the end of the sentence.
nuanceJapanese: 前置詞は at で、the も必要。in same time とは言わない。ふつう文末に置く。

meaning: Used to say yes when someone asks to do or borrow something.
cue: A friend asks to use your charger.
reply: Be my guest. It's on the desk.
replyJapanese: どうぞ。机の上にあるよ。
transferCue: A visitor asks if she can open the window.
transferReply: Be my guest. It is warm in here.
transferReplyJapanese: どうぞ。この部屋は暑いですよね。
nuance: A friendly yes when someone asks Can I ...? It is a fixed phrase, so my never changes.
nuanceJapanese: Can I ...? と頼まれたときの、感じのよい承諾。決まった言い回しなので、my は変えない。

meaning: Used as a kind reply when someone sneezes.
japanese: （くしゃみをした人に）お大事に。
cue: A classmate sneezes next to you.
reply: Bless you! Do you need a tissue?
replyJapanese: お大事に。ティッシュ、いる？
transferCue: Your manager sneezes three times in a meeting.
transferReply: Bless you! That sounds like a cold.
transferReplyJapanese: お大事に。風邪のようですね。
nuance: Say it straight after a sneeze, not after a cough. The usual answer is Thank you.
nuanceJapanese: くしゃみの直後に言う。咳には使わない。言われたら Thank you と返すのがふつう。

meaning: Without planning or meaning to.
cue: Explain how a glass got broken.
reply: I dropped the glass by accident. I'm so sorry.
replyJapanese: うっかりグラスを落としてしまいました。本当にすみません。
transferCue: Say how you found a nice café.
transferReply: We found this café by accident last summer.
transferReplyJapanese: このカフェは去年の夏、偶然見つけました。
nuance: No article: not by an accident. The opposite is on purpose.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けず、by an accident とは言わない。反対は on purpose。

meaning: With your own hands, without the help of a machine.
cue: Your washing machine is broken.
reply: I washed all my shirts by hand today.
replyJapanese: 今日はシャツを全部、手で洗いました。
transferCue: Show someone a birthday card from a friend.
transferReply: She made this card by hand for my birthday.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は私の誕生日に、このカードを手作りしてくれました。
nuance: No article and no plural: not by the hand or by hands. A thing made this way is handmade.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞も複数形も使わず、by the hand や by hands とは言わない。こうして作った物は handmade と言う。

meaning: Wrongly, without meaning to.
cue: You sent an email to the wrong person.
reply: Sorry, I sent you that email by mistake.
replyJapanese: すみません、あのメールは間違って送ってしまいました。
transferCue: Someone picked up the wrong umbrella.
transferReply: I think you took my umbrella by mistake.
transferReplyJapanese: 間違えて私の傘を持っていかれたようです。
nuance: No article: not by a mistake. Use it when you got something wrong; by accident also covers plain bad luck.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けず、by a mistake とは言わない。思い違いや取り違えに使う。by accident は単なる不運にも使える。

meaning: Without anyone helping me.
cue: A friend asks who painted your room.
reply: I painted my room by myself.
replyJapanese: 部屋は自分ひとりで塗ったよ。
transferCue: Ask for help with a heavy table.
transferReply: I can't carry this table by myself.
transferReplyJapanese: このテーブルは、ひとりでは運べません。
nuance: The word changes with the person: by yourself, by himself, by herself. It can also mean alone, with nobody else there.
nuanceJapanese: 人に合わせて by yourself、by himself、by herself と変わる。「ほかに誰もいなくて、ひとりで」の意味にもなる。

meaning: Get a cold and start to feel ill.
cue: A friend is going out with wet hair.
reply: Dry your hair, or you'll catch a cold.
replyJapanese: 髪を乾かしなよ。風邪ひくよ。
transferCue: Explain why you missed a lesson.
transferReply: I caught a cold and stayed in bed.
transferReplyJapanese: 風邪をひいて、寝ていました。
nuance: Catch is irregular: caught. Catch a cold is the start of the illness; after that you have a cold.
nuanceJapanese: catch は不規則変化で、過去形は caught。catch a cold はひき始めを表し、ひいている状態は have a cold と言う。

meaning: Decide something different from what you decided before.
japanese: 考えを変える。気が変わる。
cue: You no longer want to go out tonight.
reply: I've changed my mind. Let's stay in tonight.
replyJapanese: 気が変わった。今夜は家にいよう。
transferCue: A customer is not sure about the colour of a coat.
transferReply: You can bring it back if you change your mind.
transferReplyJapanese: 気が変わったら、返品できますよ。
nuance: Your changes with the person: I changed my mind. Use about for the topic: change your mind about the trip.
nuanceJapanese: your は人に合わせて変える：I changed my mind。話題は about で示す：change your mind about the trip。

meaning: Be more important than anything else.
japanese: 何よりも大切である。最優先である。
cue: Explain why you leave work on time.
reply: My family comes first, so I leave at five.
replyJapanese: 家族が第一なので、5時に退社します。
transferCue: A teacher talks about school trips.
transferReply: Safety always comes first on our trips.
transferReplyJapanese: 遠足では、いつも安全が第一です。
nuance: The important thing is the subject: Family comes first. In a race, come first means win.
nuanceJapanese: 大切なものを主語にする：Family comes first。競走では come first は「1位になる」の意味。

meaning: Become real after being only a hope or a dream.
japanese: （夢や願いが）かなう。実現する。
cue: A friend finally opened her own shop.
reply: Her dream came true after ten years.
replyJapanese: 彼女の夢は、10年かかってかないました。
transferCue: Write a message in a friend's birthday card.
transferReply: I hope all your wishes come true this year.
transferReplyJapanese: 今年、あなたの願いがすべてかないますように。
nuance: The dream or wish is the subject: not I came true my dream. Come is irregular: came.
nuanceJapanese: 夢や願いを主語にする。I came true my dream とは言わない。come は不規則変化で、過去形は came。

meaning: Without stopping, through the day and the night.
cue: A team had a very close deadline.
reply: We worked day and night to finish it.
replyJapanese: 仕上げるために、昼も夜も働きました。
transferCue: Describe the busy road outside your flat.
transferReply: Cars go past my window day and night.
transferReplyJapanese: 車が昼も夜も、窓の外を通ります。
nuance: No article and no plural: not days and nights. Night and day means the same.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞も複数形も使わず、days and nights とは言わない。night and day も同じ意味。

meaning: Wash the clothes and towels that need cleaning.
cue: Say what you do on Sunday mornings.
reply: I usually do the laundry on Sunday mornings.
replyJapanese: 洗濯はたいてい、日曜の朝にします。
transferCue: Ask a housemate about the chores.
transferReply: Did you do the laundry, or shall I?
transferReplyJapanese: 洗濯した？ それとも私がやろうか？
nuance: The verb is do, not make or wash. British speakers often say do the washing instead.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞は do で、make や wash は使わない。イギリスでは do the washing と言うことも多い。

meaning: Be successful or get good results.
japanese: うまくいく。良い結果を出す。
cue: Tell a friend about your job interview.
reply: I think I did well in the interview.
replyJapanese: 面接はうまくいったと思う。
transferCue: A teacher gives a parent good news.
transferReply: Your daughter is doing well in maths.
transferReplyJapanese: 娘さんは数学がよくできていますよ。
nuance: Use well, not good: not I did good. British speakers do well in an exam; Americans do well on a test.
nuanceJapanese: well を使い、I did good とは言わない。試験には、イギリス英語で in、アメリカ英語で on を使う。

meaning: Try as hard as you can.
japanese: 全力を尽くす。最善を尽くす。
cue: A friend is nervous before a race.
reply: Just do your best. You'll be fine.
replyJapanese: とにかくベストを尽くして。きっと大丈夫だよ。
transferCue: Your manager asks for a report by Friday.
transferReply: I'll do my best to finish by Friday.
transferReplyJapanese: 金曜までに終わるよう、最善を尽くします。
frame: Do your best to do something
nuance: Your changes with the person: I did my best. To cheer someone on before an event, Good luck is more common.
nuanceJapanese: your は人に合わせて変える：I did my best。本番前の「がんばって」には、Good luck のほうがふつう。

meaning: Together in the same place, not by phone or online.
japanese: 直接会って。面と向かって。
cue: A problem is hard to explain by email.
reply: Can we talk about this face to face?
replyJapanese: この件は、直接会って話せますか。
transferCue: You only knew a friend online before.
transferReply: We met face to face for the first time yesterday.
transferReplyJapanese: 昨日、初めて直接会いました。
nuance: No articles: not face to the face. Before a noun it takes hyphens: a face-to-face meeting.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けず、face to the face とは言わない。名詞の前ではハイフンでつなぐ：a face-to-face meeting。

meaning: Begin sleeping, often without planning to.
cue: Explain why you missed the end of the film.
reply: I fell asleep before the film ended.
replyJapanese: 映画が終わる前に、寝てしまいました。
transferCue: Describe a baby on car journeys.
transferReply: The baby always falls asleep in the car.
transferReplyJapanese: 赤ちゃんは車の中で、いつも寝てしまいます。
nuance: Fall is irregular: fell, fallen. It often happens by itself, such as on a train; go to sleep is something you choose.
nuanceJapanese: fall は不規則変化で fell、fallen。電車の中などで、つい眠ってしまうときによく使う。go to sleep は自分から眠ること。

meaning: Used to tell someone they are welcome to do something.
japanese: 遠慮なく〜してください。ご自由にどうぞ。
cue: You finish explaining a new plan to your team.
reply: Feel free to ask me any questions.
replyJapanese: 質問があれば、遠慮なく聞いてください。
transferCue: A friend is staying at your flat.
transferReply: Feel free to take anything from the fridge.
transferReplyJapanese: 冷蔵庫のものは、何でも自由に食べてね。
nuance: Followed by to and a verb. You say it to another person, not about yourself. Please feel free is a little more polite.
nuanceJapanese: 後ろに to と動詞を続ける。相手に向けて言い、自分のことには使わない。Please feel free とすると少し丁寧になる。

meaning: Feel that you are not well.
japanese: 気分が悪い。具合が悪い。
cue: You are at school and your stomach hurts.
reply: I feel sick. Can I go home early?
replyJapanese: 気分が悪いです。早退してもいいですか。
transferCue: A boy ate too much at a party.
transferReply: He felt sick after eating all that cake.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はあのケーキを全部食べて、気持ちが悪くなりました。
nuance: In British English feel sick usually means you may vomit, and feel ill is the general word. Americans use feel sick for both.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語では、feel sick はふつう吐き気がすること。体調不良全般には feel ill を使う。アメリカ英語ではどちらにも feel sick を使う。

meaning: Feel sad about your own problems and think they are unfair.
japanese: 自分を哀れむ。くよくよする。
cue: A friend lost a match and has stayed in bed all day.
reply: Stop feeling sorry for yourself and come out.
replyJapanese: くよくよしてないで、出ておいでよ。
transferCue: Say how you felt after failing a test.
transferReply: I felt sorry for myself for a few days.
transferReplyJapanese: 何日かは、自分がかわいそうに思えて落ち込んでいました。
nuance: With yourself or myself it means self-pity and sounds a little critical. With another person it means you feel sad for them.
nuanceJapanese: yourself や myself を続けると「自分を哀れむ」の意味で、やや批判的に響く。ほかの人を続けると「気の毒に思う」の意味になる。

meaning: Used to introduce the first thing you want to say or do.
japanese: まず第一に。何よりもまず。
cue: Start a meeting with new team members.
reply: First of all, let me introduce myself.
replyJapanese: まず、自己紹介をさせてください。
transferCue: A friend asks how to make curry.
transferReply: First of all, cut the onions into small pieces.
transferReplyJapanese: まず最初に、玉ねぎを小さく切ってね。
nuance: Put it at the start, with a comma after it. At first is different: it means in the beginning, before something changed.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置き、あとにコンマを打つ。at first は別の表現で、「最初のうちは（その後変わった）」という意味。

meaning: Costing you no money.
cue: Tell a friend about a museum offer.
reply: Children can get in for free on Sundays.
replyJapanese: 日曜日は、子どもは無料で入れます。
transferCue: A kind neighbour helped you.
transferReply: My neighbour fixed my bike for free.
transferReplyJapanese: 近所の人が、ただで自転車を直してくれました。
nuance: Informal. Free alone also works: Children get in free. In careful writing, free of charge is safer.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた言い方。free だけでもよい：Children get in free。改まった文章では free of charge が無難。

meaning: Because you enjoy it, not for money or work.
japanese: 楽しみのために。趣味で。
cue: Someone asks if painting is your job.
reply: No, I only paint for fun.
replyJapanese: いいえ、趣味で描いているだけです。
transferCue: Explain why you joined a running club.
transferReply: I joined the running club just for fun.
transferReplyJapanese: ランニングクラブには、ただ楽しみで入りました。
nuance: No article: not for a fun. What do you do for fun? is a common way to ask about hobbies.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けず、for a fun とは言わない。What do you do for fun? は趣味をたずねる定番の言い方。

meaning: Offered for people to buy.
japanese: 売りに出ている。売り物である。
cue: You notice a sign outside a neighbour's house.
reply: The house next door is for sale.
replyJapanese: 隣の家が売りに出ています。
transferCue: A customer asks about a painting on a café wall.
transferReply: Sorry, that painting is not for sale.
transferReplyJapanese: すみません、あの絵は売り物ではありません。
nuance: For sale means you can buy it. On sale often means at a lower price, especially in American English.
nuanceJapanese: for sale は「売り物である」という意味。on sale は、とくにアメリカ英語で「値下げ中」を表すことが多い。

meaning: Without any doubt.
cue: A friend asks what time the train leaves.
reply: I don't know for sure. Let me check.
replyJapanese: はっきりとは分からない。確認するね。
transferCue: Promise to come to a friend's party.
transferReply: I'll be there on Saturday for sure.
transferReplyJapanese: 土曜日は絶対に行くよ。
nuance: Informal. It often follows know or say: I don't know for sure. As a short answer, For sure! means yes, definitely.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた言い方。know や say のあとによく使う：I don't know for sure。For sure! だけで「もちろん」という返事にもなる。

meaning: Hours when you have no work or study and can choose what to do.
cue: Ask a new colleague about hobbies.
reply: What do you like doing in your free time?
replyJapanese: 暇なときは、何をするのが好きですか。
transferCue: Explain a busy month to a friend.
transferReply: I don't have much free time this month.
transferReplyJapanese: 今月は、あまり自由な時間がないんだ。
frame: In your free time / have free time
nuance: No article and no plural: not a free time. The preposition is in: in my free time.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞も複数形も使わず、a free time とは言わない。前置詞は in で、in my free time と言う。

meaning: Starting now and continuing into the future.
japanese: これからは。今後ずっと。
cue: You were late for work again.
reply: From now on, I'll leave home at seven.
replyJapanese: これからは、7時に家を出ます。
transferCue: A teacher announces a new class rule.
transferReply: Phones must stay in your bags from now on.
transferReplyJapanese: 今後は、携帯電話はかばんに入れておいてください。
nuance: It marks a lasting change, so use will or the present, not the past. Keep on: from now alone does not mean this.
nuanceJapanese: これから続く変化を表すので、will や現在形と使い、過去形とは使わない。on は省けず、from now だけではこの意味にならない。

meaning: Find paid work and begin doing it.
cue: Share good news about your sister.
reply: My sister got a job at a bank.
replyJapanese: 姉が銀行に就職しました。
transferCue: Talk about your plans after university.
transferReply: I hope to get a job in a hotel.
transferReplyJapanese: ホテルで仕事に就きたいと思っています。
frame: Get a job at / in a place
nuance: Job needs a: not get job. Work has no article, so say find work, not find a work.
nuanceJapanese: job には a が必要で、get job とは言わない。work には冠詞を付けず、find work と言う（find a work は誤り）。

meaning: Become better than before.
cue: Encourage a friend who is learning the guitar.
reply: You're getting better every week.
replyJapanese: 毎週うまくなっているよ。
transferCue: Someone asks about your cold.
transferReply: My cold got better after two days in bed.
transferReplyJapanese: 2日寝ていたら、風邪が良くなりました。
nuance: Better is already a comparative, so never say more better. Use at for a skill: get better at cooking. The opposite is get worse.
nuanceJapanese: better はすでに比較級なので、more better とは言わない。技能には at を使う：get better at cooking。反対は get worse。

meaning: Leave a place or start a journey.
japanese: 出発する。そろそろ行く。
cue: It is late and you are still at a friend's house.
reply: It's late. I should get going.
replyJapanese: もう遅いね。そろそろ行かなくちゃ。
transferCue: Your family is slow to leave for the airport.
transferReply: Let's get going, or we'll miss the flight.
transferReplyJapanese: もう出よう。飛行機に乗り遅れるよ。
nuance: Informal. I should get going is a soft, friendly way to say you need to leave.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた言い方。I should get going は、そろそろ帰ると伝えるやわらかい表現。

meaning: Lose your way so that you cannot find where to go.
cue: Explain why you arrived late at a friend's new flat.
reply: Sorry, I got lost on the way here.
replyJapanese: ごめん、来る途中で道に迷っちゃった。
transferCue: Warn a visitor about the old town.
transferReply: Take a map. It's easy to get lost there.
transferReplyJapanese: 地図を持って行ってください。あそこは迷いやすいですから。
nuance: Get lost is the moment you lose your way; be lost is the state after. As an order, Get lost! is a rude way to say go away.
nuanceJapanese: get lost は迷う瞬間、be lost は迷っている状態を表す。Get lost! と命令形で言うと「あっちへ行け」という失礼な表現になる。

meaning: Become someone's husband or wife.
cue: Share news about your brother.
reply: My brother is getting married in June.
replyJapanese: 兄が6月に結婚します。
transferCue: Someone asks how long your parents have been together.
transferReply: My parents got married thirty years ago.
transferReplyJapanese: 両親は30年前に結婚しました。
nuance: Use to, not with: She got married to a doctor. Without get, marry takes the person directly: She married a doctor.
nuanceJapanese: 前置詞は to で、with は使わない：She got married to a doctor。get を使わない marry は、相手を直接続ける：She married a doctor。

meaning: Begin doing something.
cue: Everyone has arrived for the meeting.
reply: Everyone's here, so let's get started.
replyJapanese: 全員そろったので、始めましょう。
transferCue: You have a lot of homework tonight.
transferReply: I need to get started on my homework.
transferReplyJapanese: 宿題に取りかからないといけません。
nuance: Let's get started is a common way to open a meeting or lesson. Use on or with before the task: get started on the report.
nuanceJapanese: Let's get started は、会議や授業を始めるときの定番表現。取りかかる対象は on か with で示す：get started on the report。

meaning: Come to know a person or place well, little by little.
japanese: だんだんよく知るようになる。親しくなる。
cue: Talk about a new neighbour.
reply: I'd like to get to know her better.
replyJapanese: 彼女のことを、もっとよく知りたいです。
transferCue: Describe your first month in a new city.
transferReply: I'm slowly getting to know the city.
transferReplyJapanese: 少しずつ、この街のことが分かってきました。
nuance: It is a slow process, not one moment. For the first time you see someone, use meet: I met her in May.
nuanceJapanese: 一瞬の出来事ではなく、時間をかけて知っていく過程を表す。初めて会うことには meet を使う：I met her in May。

meaning: Travel to another country.
japanese: 海外へ行く。外国に行く。
cue: Say what you want to do next summer.
reply: I want to go abroad next summer.
replyJapanese: 来年の夏は、海外に行きたいです。
transferCue: Talk about your grandmother's first trip overseas.
transferReply: My grandmother went abroad for the first time last year.
transferReplyJapanese: 祖母は去年、初めて海外に行きました。
nuance: No preposition: not go to abroad. Abroad is an adverb, like home in go home.
nuanceJapanese: 前置詞は不要で、go to abroad とは言わない。abroad は go home の home と同じく副詞。

meaning: Travel around a place to see its famous sights.
japanese: 観光に行く。名所を見て回る。
cue: Plan a free day in Kyoto with a friend.
reply: Let's go sightseeing in Kyoto tomorrow.
replyJapanese: 明日は京都を観光しよう。
transferCue: Tell a colleague about your weekend in London.
transferReply: We went sightseeing and took a lot of photos.
transferReplyJapanese: 観光をして、写真をたくさん撮りました。
nuance: Use in before the place, not to: go sightseeing in Rome. No article: not go to a sightseeing.
nuanceJapanese: 場所の前は to ではなく in：go sightseeing in Rome。冠詞は付けず、go to a sightseeing とは言わない。

meaning: Start sleeping, usually when you choose to.
cue: A child is still reading at eleven o'clock.
reply: Close your book and go to sleep now.
replyJapanese: 本を閉じて、もう寝なさい。
transferCue: Explain why you look tired.
transferReply: I couldn't go to sleep until two last night.
transferReplyJapanese: 昨夜は2時まで寝つけませんでした。
nuance: No article: not go to the sleep. Go to bed is getting into bed; go to sleep is the moment sleep starts.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けず、go to the sleep とは言わない。go to bed はベッドに入ること、go to sleep は眠り始めること。

meaning: Have problems and not happen as planned.
japanese: うまくいかなくなる。失敗する。
cue: Describe a bad holiday.
reply: Everything went wrong on the first day.
replyJapanese: 初日から、何もかもうまくいきませんでした。
transferCue: A colleague is nervous before an event.
transferReply: Don't worry. Nothing will go wrong tonight.
transferReplyJapanese: 心配しないで。今夜は何も問題は起きませんよ。
nuance: The plan or event is the subject, often something, everything or nothing. Go is irregular: went, gone.
nuanceJapanese: 計画や出来事を主語にし、something、everything、nothing がよく使われる。go は不規則変化で went、gone。

meaning: Used just before you share surprising news.
cue: You passed your driving test. Tell a friend.
reply: Guess what! I passed my driving test.
replyJapanese: ねえ聞いて！ 運転免許の試験に受かったよ。
transferCue: Tell your family about a visitor.
transferReply: Guess what? Grandma is coming on Friday.
transferReplyJapanese: ねえ、聞いて。金曜日におばあちゃんが来るよ。
nuance: Informal. You do not wait for a real guess; the listener just says What? and you tell the news.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現。本当に当ててもらうわけではなく、相手が What? と返したら、すぐに話を続ける。

meaning: Not know something at all.
japanese: まったく分からない。見当もつかない。
cue: A housemate asks where the keys are.
reply: I have no idea where your keys are.
replyJapanese: あなたの鍵がどこにあるか、まったく分からないよ。
transferCue: Describe a surprise party for a friend.
transferReply: She had no idea about the party.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はパーティーのことを、まったく知りませんでした。
frame: Have no idea where / why / how …
nuance: Stronger than I don't know. After it, keep statement word order: where your keys are, not where are your keys.
nuanceJapanese: I don't know より強い。あとに疑問詞を続けるときは平叙文の語順にする：where your keys are（where are your keys ではない）。

meaning: In a few scattered places.
japanese: あちこちに。ところどころに。
cue: Describe your garden in spring.
reply: There are yellow flowers here and there.
replyJapanese: 黄色い花が、あちこちに咲いています。
transferCue: A teacher comments on your essay.
transferReply: I found a few small mistakes here and there.
transferReplyJapanese: ところどころに、小さな間違いがいくつかありました。
nuance: The order is fixed: here comes first, not there and here. It suggests a few scattered places, not everywhere.
nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定で here が先。there and here とは言わない。「至る所」ではなく、ところどころに少しある様子を表す。

meaning: Keep your hand in another person's hand.
cue: Describe an old couple in the park.
reply: They always hold hands when they walk.
replyJapanese: 二人は歩くとき、いつも手をつないでいます。
transferCue: A teacher takes small children across the road.
transferReply: Hold hands with your partner, please.
transferReplyJapanese: 隣のお友だちと手をつないでください。
nuance: Hands is plural, with no article and no my or your: not hold a hand. Hold is irregular: held.
nuanceJapanese: hands は複数形で、冠詞や my、your は付けない。hold a hand とは言わない。hold は不規則変化で、過去形は held。

meaning: Stop breathing for a short time.
cue: A nurse is about to take an X-ray.
reply: Please hold your breath for ten seconds.
replyJapanese: 10秒間、息を止めてください。
transferCue: Describe swimming under water.
transferReply: I held my breath and swam under the boat.
transferReplyJapanese: 息を止めて、ボートの下を泳ぎました。
nuance: Breath is the noun; breathe, with an e, is the verb. Your changes with the person: I held my breath.
nuanceJapanese: breath は名詞で、動詞は e の付く breathe。your は人に合わせて変える：I held my breath。

meaning: Used to ask why something is so.
cue: A friend arrives an hour early.
reply: How come you're here so early?
replyJapanese: なんでこんなに早く来たの？
transferCue: A colleague did not come to the team lunch.
transferReply: How come you didn't join us for lunch?
transferReplyJapanese: どうしてお昼に来なかったんですか。
nuance: Informal. The word order stays like a statement: How come you left? not How come did you leave?
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現。あとは平叙文の語順のまま：How come you left? と言い、How come did you leave? とは言わない。

meaning: Used to say yes when you are not completely sure.
japanese: そう思います。たぶんそうです。
cue: Someone asks if the shop is open today.
reply: I think so, but let me check online.
replyJapanese: そう思いますが、ネットで確認してみます。
transferCue: A friend asks if Ken is coming to the party.
transferReply: I think so. He said yes last week.
transferReplyJapanese: たぶん来ると思う。先週、行くって言ってたから。
nuance: So stands for the whole idea, so do not say I think it. The negative is usually I don't think so.
nuanceJapanese: so が前の内容全体を受けるので、I think it とは言わない。否定はふつう I don't think so。
